gates.title: Per-image licensing, archive capture, and public availability
gates.reason: The file-specific record is complete: creator, host, access method, hashes, capturer's collection statement, and Microsoft's general screenshot guideline. It shows no file-specific licence. The capture layer rests on an informal permission from the capturer; the Microsoft software layer is unresolved. Per R14, unknown rights stay blocked.
gates.boundary_compliance: No account, payment, terms acceptance, CAPTCHA, watermark removal or gated download. MobyGames returned 403 and the Xbox Wire image looped through redirects; neither was worked around.
gates.review_question: Rights review: may this capture be used on screen (Microsoft screenshot guideline versus a fair-use commentary basis), and is the capturer's informal credit-requested permission sufficient?

supporting_checks.claim: The image shows Microsoft Solitaire with a green playfield.
supporting_checks.evidence: source/original.png inspected at full 1920x1080. The guest window has title 'Solitaire', a Game/Help menu bar, a green playfield, a card deck with Queens on the foundations and Kings on the tableau, and a status bar reading 'Score: 383 Time: 311'.

supporting_checks.claim: The operating system is Windows 3.1, not 3.0 or Windows for Workgroups 3.11.
evidence: The Internet Archive original file is named 'Solitaire (Windows 3.1).png'.

In the capture, the running VM window is titled 'Windows 3.1 [Running] - Oracle VirtualBox'. The selected VirtualBox Manager entry is 'Windows 3.1 / Running', listed separately from VMs named 'Windows 3.0' and 'Windows 3.11 for Workgroups'.

Limitation: VM names are set by the user. In the capturer's own Windows 3.0 capture (archive.org item solitaire-on-windows-3.0), VirtualBox's type field reads 'Windows 3.1' for the VM named 'Windows 3.0'. Nothing visible inside the guest screen (no About box, no version string) independently establishes 3.1.
supporting_checks.consequence: Captions may say 'Windows 3.1 Solitaire (capture labelled Windows 3.1 by its author)'. Do not present pixel-level version proof.

supporting_checks.claim: SCRIPT.md:593 — 'Windows came bundled with Solitaire and Minesweeper'.
supporting_checks.evidence: Microsoft Windows User's Guide version 3.1, April 1992 (PC21669-0492): p.73 (leaf 99) says Setup copied Solitaire and Minesweeper to the hard disk; p.540 (leaf 566) lists SOL.EXE and WINMINE.EXE. The Windows 3.0 User's Guide (1989) lists Solitaire and Reversi instead, so Minesweeper bundling applies from 3.1.

No R gate assigns this claim to HIST-19, and no primary source found here states Solitaire's implementation language. The ticket only requires that this still not imply Solitaire was written in VB. It does not: the frame carries no caption or VB labelling.

supporting_checks.claim: SCRIPT.md:579 visual cue — 'Screenshots of 90s shareware card games — Solitaire, Hearts, FreeCell'.
supporting_checks.evidence: Microsoft Solitaire shipped with Windows (User's Guide p.73); it was not shareware. The narration at line 593 already says 'bundled'. Only the visual-direction note groups it under 'shareware'.
